column2: is an illegal target when Fiery Annihilation begins to resolve
column3: Inconsistent with the other rulings on a target described by another target that has become illegal but is still there (ruling 2024-11-08; work item ruling-conflicts-4, case 1, conclusion D; work item user-questions-nov7, Part A): Yosei, the Morning Star 2017-11-17 ('If the player becomes an illegal target, the target permanents are tapped, but the player doesn't skip their untap step.'), Down for Repairs 2022-10-07 and Run Away Together 2022-06-10, 2024-07-26 and 2025-11-17 ('can still determine its controller only to check whether the other creature is a legal target') still check the dependent target against the illegal one and affect it; the CR draws no line between attachment and control (608.2b's last sentences separate no kinds of information; 109.3 lists 'an object’s owner or controller' and 'what an Aura enchants' together; 115.9b and 800.4i treat players and objects alike), and Fiery Annihilation is the only card whose second target is described by attachment to the first; set aside as inconsistent by the user's decision of Nov 7 (register dependent-target-checked-against-an-illegal-target, decided; logged in docs/RULING_DISCREPANCIES.md); the engine exiles the Equipment still attached to an illegal creature (tested in tests/rulings/illegal_anchor_targets.rs, fiery_annihilation_exiles_equipment_still_attached_to_an_illegal_creature)
